text:
dani: Heads-up: onboarding sample app is throwing schema errors when using function-calling + json_mode. Weird parity between JS/py SDKs — py silently accepts numbers-as-strings, JS fails.

liam: can you paste the exact failure? the details matter (type coercion vs truncated streams).

dani: minimal log (local dev):
```
Request: chat.generate {model: 'rw-4', function_call: true, json_mode: true}
Model returns: {"action":"create_invoice","args":{"amount":"100","due_days":"30"}}
JS SDK Ajv error: data.args.amount should be number but is string
Py SDK: pydantic coerces "100" -> 100 and proceeds
```
This comes up in the sample invoicing app during onboarding; some LLM outputs numbers as strings (we've seen amounts come back quoted), and our JS validator is strict.

anya: I remember a change: we flipped Ajv "coerceTypes" to false to avoid silent coercion masking model bugs. But the sample app expects coercion for backward compatibility with older models that emit strings. That explains parity and customer confusion.

liam: is this happening only in streaming or also non-streamed?

dani: both. But streaming makes the error surface earlier in the pipeline and the UX is worse (partial UI render then crash). The core issue is schema strictness rather than auth/retry. That said, retries can concatenate representations which can exacerbate parser confusion if combined with streaming.

anya: options:
- revert Ajv.coerceTypes to true (fast but risky: hides model produce-bad-type bugs).
- add an SDK helper that accepts a "lenient: true" option for json_mode/function_call to coerce basic types (string->number, "true"->bool) only for primitive schemas.
- update onboarding sample to include an explicit schema that accepts both number and string for amount (oneOf: [number, string]) and add a transform step that normalizes types.
- add a telemetry event when coercion happens so we can monitor model quality instead of silently hiding it.

liam: I like the middle ground: ship a small helper in JS SDK `schema.normalizeTypes()` that runs only when the customer opts in (default remains strict). Also emit telemetry `json_mode.coercion.v1` with model, endpoint, and normalized fields (hashed) to track prevalence.

dani: sample app changes: change onboarding README to recommend either: use `schema.strict: false` in dev, or define schema with flexible types. But many users copy the sample verbatim so better if SDK helps by default for first-run (to reduce friction). Maybe default to lenient for self-serve onboarding UX but require explicit opt-in for enterprise? That gets messy.

anya: process note: we must keep API behavior stable for enterprises. Proposal: default remains strict; onboarding CLI (redwood init sample-app) will pass `rw.devex.coerce_onboarding=true` in env for local runs. SDK respects that env var to enable normalizeTypes only for onboarding-run. That keeps server behavior unchanged.

liam: technical note for JS helper: implement a shallow coercion pass that walks schema properties and coerces primitives if the schema expects number/bool but value is string matching regex. Avoid deep structural rewrites. Add unit tests covering edge cases: "000" vs "00x" etc.

anya: py-sdk parity: pydantic currently coerces aggressively. We'll add a strict mode in pydantic models and opt it in for enterprise by default; add a helper `coerce_types=True` to match JS. File a parity task to align defaults.

release-bot: canary: js-sdk/0.13.0-beta (includes schema.normalizeTypes helper) rolling to staging. Tests: unit ok, integration pending.

dani: PRs:
- https://git.redwood/devex/sdk-js/pulls/501 (adds schema.normalizeTypes + telemetry)
- https://git.redwood/devex/onboarding/pulls/78 (sets env var for sample app local runs)
- https://git.redwood/devex/sdk-py/pulls/220 (adds opt-in strict mode and coerce flag)

liam: docs: add a section "When your function args are numbers but model returns strings" under docs/devex/json-mode.md explaining coercion options and showing a small helper snippet:
```
client.chat.generate({json_mode:true, function_call:true, schema:{ /*...*/ }, coerce_types:true})
```
Don't encourage leaving coercion on in prod.

anya: tests: add a regression that simulates older models that produce quoted numbers and verify onboarding sample works with env var enabled. Also add a parity check to ensure JS/Py helpers behave the same with coerce flag set.

dani: customer impact: low severity but high friction for new users. I'd like the staging canary to run for 48h and then we decide whether to backport a small patch to 0.12.x.

liam: ok. I'll merge the helper PR once CI green. @dani please run the onboarding flow locally with the canary and paste traces if anything else pops up.

release-bot: canary complete: js-sdk/0.13.0-beta - telemetry shows ~2% of onboarding runs required coercion.

anya: perfect. filing follow-ups: DEVEX-2301 (parity defaults), DEVEX-2302 (onboarding docs), DEVEX-2303 (coercion telemetry dashboard).

dani: thanks all. tagging @devex for visibility.
